revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Football Plays
revealWordProblem.text:
To make a first down, a football team must gain at least 10 yards from where it started, called the line of scrimmage. During one series of plays a team had a 10-yard loss, a 4-yard gain, a 3-yard loss, and a 21-yard gain.
Question: Did the football team make a first down? How far are they from the line of scrimmage?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A football field marked with the line of scrimmage, the first down line, and the 10-yard gain between them.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Write each play as an integer, with losses negative and gains positive: −10, +4, −3, +21. Add them in order: −10 + 4 = −6, then −6 + (−3) = −9, then −9 + 21 = +12. The team ended 12 yards past the line of scrimmage. Since 12 is at least 10, yes — they made the first down, with 2 yards to spare.

questions.stem: In Reykjavik the temperature was -9°C. What is the opposite of -9?
questions.explanation: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side, so the opposite of -9 is 9.
choiceFeedback: A number cannot be its own opposite unless it is 0. The opposite of a negative number is on the other side of 0, so it is positive.
Zero is its own opposite, but it is not the opposite of -9 — it is 9 units away from -9, not on the far side of 0.
Doubling the distance from 0 is not the same as crossing to the other side. The opposite keeps the distance 9 and only changes the direction.
hints: 'Opposite' means the same distance from 0, but on the other side of 0.
-9 sits 9 units to the LEFT of 0. Count 9 units to the RIGHT of 0 instead.
Keep the 9 exactly the same and change only the direction, which means changing only the sign.
questions.stemEs: En Reikiavik la temperatura era -9°C. ¿Cuál es el opuesto de -9?
questions.explanationEs: El opuesto de un número está a la misma distancia de 0 pero del otro lado, así que el opuesto de -9 es 9.
hintsEs: 'Opuesto' significa la misma distancia del 0, pero al otro lado del 0.
-9 está a 9 unidades a la IZQUIERDA del 0. Cuenta 9 unidades a la DERECHA del 0 en su lugar.

The opposite of a number is one specific number, not a whole group of them. Every number has exactly one opposite.
Zero does have an opposite. Since its distance from 0 is 0, it lands right back on itself.

steps: 1. Integers: Positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero (..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...)
2. Opposites: Numbers that are the same distance from 0 in opposite directions (e.g. -5 and 5)

reviewHighlights.watchOut: The most common mistake in this lesson is thinking that the opposite of a negative integer is still negative — for example, saying the opposite of -7 is -7, or that the opposite of -12 is -24. Opposites are the same DISTANCE from 0 but on OPPOSITE sides of 0, so taking an opposite always changes the direction and never changes the distance: the opposite of -7 is 7 and the opposite of -12 is 12. The one exception is 0, which is 0 units from itself and is therefore its own opposite. Before you submit, count the units from 0 and check that your answer is on the other side.

level3.explanation: Write each play as an integer: -10, 4, -3, 21. Combining them gives -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12, so the team ends 12 yards past the line of scrimmage.
choiceFeedback: The 4-yard gain got left out of the count. Every play changes the team's position, gains and losses alike.
The 3-yard loss was counted as a gain here. A loss moves the team backward, so it is a negative integer.
This adds all four plays as if every one were a gain. Losses have to be written as negative integers before you combine them.
hints: The line of scrimmage is 0. Which plays move the team below 0, and which move it above?
Write all four plays as integers first: gains are positive and losses are negative.
Combine -10, 4, -3, and 21 in order, keeping every sign. Where do you land compared to 0?
level3.stemEs: Un equipo de fútbol americano empieza en la línea de golpeo, que es 0. En una serie tuvo una pérdida de 10 yardas, una ganancia de 4 yardas, una pérdida de 3 yardas y una ganancia de 21 yardas. ¿Dónde termina la serie?
level3.explanationEs: Escribe cada jugada como entero: -10, 4, -3, 21. Al combinarlos: -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12, así que el equipo termina 12 yardas más allá de la línea de golpeo.
hintsEs: La línea de golpeo es 0. ¿Cuáles jugadas mueven al equipo debajo de 0 y cuáles por encima?
Escribe primero las cuatro jugadas como enteros: las ganancias son positivas y las pérdidas negativas.
Combina -10, 4, -3 y 21 en orden, conservando cada signo. ¿Dónde caes en comparación con 0?

level3.prompt: Describe two different real-world situations that use negative integers. For each one, tell exactly what 0 means in that situation, write one negative integer it could produce, and explain what the opposite of that integer would mean in the same situation.
level3.promptEs: Describe dos situaciones del mundo real distintas que usen enteros negativos. Para cada una, di exactamente qué significa 0 en esa situación, escribe un entero negativo que podría producir y explica qué significaría el opuesto de ese entero en la misma situación.
level3.sentenceFrame: My first situation is ___. In it, 0 means ___, so ___ would represent ___. The opposite of that integer is ___, which would mean ___.
level3.hint: Pick situations where something can be measured both above and below a natural starting point.
hints: Think about places where a measurement can go both above and below a starting point: elevation, temperature, money, football yardage.
Name the starting point out loud — that is your 0. Then a quantity below it is your negative integer.
For the opposite, keep the same distance from 0 and cross to the other side, then say what that new number means in your story.
level3.explanation: Every situation that uses negative integers has a chosen zero. With elevation, 0 is sea level, so -30 meters means 30 meters below the surface and its opposite, 30, means 30 meters above it. With temperature, 0 is zero degrees, so -5°C is five degrees below zero and its opposite, 5°C, is five degrees above. In both cases the opposite is the same distance from 0, just measured in the other direction, which is what makes it the mirror image of the original quantity.
level3.explanationEs: Toda situación que usa enteros negativos tiene un cero elegido. Con la elevación, 0 es el nivel del mar, así que -30 metros significa 30 metros bajo la superficie y su opuesto, 30, significa 30 metros por encima. Con la temperatura, 0 es cero grados, así que -5°C son cinco grados bajo cero y su opuesto, 5°C, son cinco grados arriba. En ambos casos el opuesto está a la misma distancia del 0, solo medido en la otra dirección, y eso lo convierte en el reflejo de la cantidad original.
hintsEs: Piensa en lugares donde una medida puede ir por encima y por debajo de un punto de partida: elevación, temperatura, dinero, yardas de fútbol americano.
Di en voz alta cuál es el punto de partida — ese es tu 0. Luego una cantidad por debajo de él es tu entero negativo.
Para el opuesto, conserva la misma distancia del 0 y cruza al otro lado, luego di qué significa ese número nuevo en tu historia.

level3.stem: Claim: “The opposite of a number is always negative.” Always, sometimes, or never true?
choices: Sometimes — it is negative only when the original number is positive
Always — that is what taking the opposite does
Never — opposites are always positive
Sometimes — it depends whether the number is a whole number
level3.explanation: Opposite means the same distance from 0 on the other side, so it flips whichever side you started on. The opposite of 7 is −7, which is negative; the opposite of −7 is 7, which is not. And 0 is its own opposite, so it is neither.
choiceFeedback: Then what is the opposite of −7? Flipping it lands on the positive side.
The opposite of 7 is −7, which is negative.
Whole or not makes no difference — the opposite of −2.5 is 2.5.
hints: Say what opposite means in terms of distance from 0.
Test it on a positive number, then on a negative one.
If one test comes out each way, which answer must it be?
level3.stemEs: Afirmación: “El opuesto de un número siempre es negativo.” ¿Siempre, a veces o nunca es cierto?
choicesEs: A veces — es negativo solo cuando el número original es positivo
Siempre — eso es lo que hace tomar el opuesto
Nunca — los opuestos siempre son positivos
A veces — depende de si el número es entero
level3.explanationEs: Opuesto significa la misma distancia desde 0 pero del otro lado, así que voltea el lado en el que empezaste. El opuesto de 7 es −7, que es negativo; el opuesto de −7 es 7, que no lo es. Y 0 es su propio opuesto, así que no es ninguno de los dos.
hintsEs: Di qué significa opuesto en términos de distancia desde 0.
Pruébalo con un número positivo y luego con uno negativo.
Si cada prueba sale distinta, ¿qué respuesta tiene que ser?

level3.stem: A diver is at −18 m and a drone is at +18 m. Priya says they are the same distance from sea level. Wes says the drone is higher, so it is farther away. Who is right?
choices: Priya — both are 18 m from 0, and distance from 0 ignores direction
Wes — +18 is greater than −18, so it must be farther
Both, because distance and height mean the same thing
Neither — you cannot compare a depth with a height
level3.explanation: Two different questions hide here. Higher compares position, and Wes is right that +18 is above −18. Farther from sea level compares distance from 0, and there they tie at 18 m. Priya answered the question that was asked.
choiceFeedback: Greater and farther-from-zero are not the same test. −18 is less than +18 yet exactly as far from 0.
They differ: one keeps direction, the other drops it.
You can — measure each one's distance from 0.
hints: Mark −18 and +18 on a number line with 0 between them.
Count the units from 0 to each mark.
Which word is the question using — higher, or farther from sea level?
level3.stemEs: Un buzo está a −18 m y un dron a +18 m. Priya dice que están a la misma distancia del nivel del mar. Wes dice que el dron está más alto, así que está más lejos. ¿Quién tiene razón?
choicesEs: Priya — ambos están a 18 m de 0, y la distancia desde 0 no toma en cuenta la dirección
Wes — +18 es mayor que −18, así que tiene que estar más lejos
Los dos, porque distancia y altura significan lo mismo
Ninguno — no se puede comparar una profundidad con una altura
level3.explanationEs: Aquí se esconden dos preguntas distintas. Más alto compara la posición, y Wes tiene razón en que +18 está por encima de −18. Más lejos del nivel del mar compara la distancia desde 0, y ahí empatan en 18 m. Priya respondió la pregunta que se hizo.
hintsEs: Marca −18 y +18 en una recta numérica con el 0 en medio.
Cuenta las unidades desde 0 hasta cada marca.
¿Qué palabra usa la pregunta — más alto o más lejos del nivel del mar?

tool.intro: Drag the point to any integer. Watch its distance from 0 and its opposite — −9°C in Reykjavik and 9°C in Toronto sit the same distance from 0 on opposite sides.
